title: every leg of CI's ubuntu job passes, and verify.sh runs each of them
description: The ubuntu job's encoding leg fails on a selection-miss fixture that prints a character a cp1252 stream cannot encode, and no local command runs that leg. Make the fixture independent of its child's stream encoding, then run the leg locally and hold the sweep's legs to both runners.
desiredOutcome: CI's ubuntu job is green on both of its sweeps, including the one on a stream that cannot spell every character, and verify.sh runs that leg too, held to CI by gate-parity

findings.issue: The sweep reader counts one literal call per line and loses a second call joined by && or ;, a call spelled through ./, a variable or an interpreter flag, and an env-prefixed call (read as an assignment); the empty-side guard never trips because the plain leg is always present, so a leg added in any of these spellings on one side only is reported as agreement.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.4-287 (e08387b4): Read every mention of the sweep on a non-comment line, split each line into its commands, treat NAME=val followed by words as a command with an env prefix, and report any mention the parser cannot resolve as a problem; cases for the env prefix and two calls on one line.

findings.issue: sweep_legs never expands loop variables, so a leg run inside a for loop comes back unresolved although report_targets resolves the same form through the same scan, which contradicts the shared reader's own docstring.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.4-287 (e08387b4): Expand a bare loop variable to one leg per loop word; a case where a looped leg agrees with the same leg written bare.

findings.issue: A call inside a subshell reads the closing parenthesis as part of the call, producing a false drift against the same call written bare.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.4-287 (e08387b4): Stop at a closing parenthesis; a subshell case.

findings.issue: Both lists of the commands verify.sh calls name the plain and selftest sweep legs but not the encoding leg verify.sh now runs, and no gate compares the document sides' legs.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.4-287 (e08387b4): Add the encoding leg to both lists.

findings.issue: The selection-miss fixture's byte echo is measured only under the sweep's encoding leg, which verify.sh --fast skips; gb6 pins the codec itself for the same reason.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.3-287 (bf011c39): Pin PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 around at least one selection-miss run, as gb6 does.

findings.issue: A ratio claim about the leg's cost in prose with no command beside it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P93.4-287 (e08387b4): State the cost without the ratio.

review.outcome: Phase review drove the encoding leg and both readers; its two meds (sweep calls lost when list-joined, env-prefixed, dot-pathed or looped) and four lows were fixed in P93.3 and P93.4 and resolved; the phase gate and verify.sh (with the encoding leg) are green, invariants found no breach. Comparing the document sides' sweep legs is left as a follow-up. [findings: 6 - 0 high, 2 med, 4 low; 6 with a recorded fix commit]

summary: The selection-miss fixtures write UTF-8 bytes like a real runner and one run of them is pinned to a cp1252 stream, so the ubuntu encoding leg and every local sweep see a named suite; verify.sh runs the sweep's encoding leg, and gate-parity reads both runners as shell and holds their sweep legs and report targets to each other, reporting any call it cannot resolve.

tasks.description: The fake runner the sm cases write (gate.py) prints a jest bullet through a text stream, so a cp1252 stream crashes it. Write its output as the bytes a real runner writes (UTF-8), independent of the child's stream encoding; check every other fixture in the file that prints a character outside cp1252. Red first with the sweep's encoding leg (tools/sweep-selftests.py --encoding cp1252) or PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 on the suite.

Also the verify.sh cost comment without a ratio, and CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md list the encoding leg.
